subject: science
passage: In 1937, a botanist at the University of Iowa carefully washed the soil from a single rye plant that had grown in a box for four months. He then measured every root he could find. His count showed that the roots of one rye plant, not counting the tiny root hairs, ______ to a combined length of more than 600 kilometers.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the verb is "roots," which is plural; "of one rye plant" and "not counting the tiny root hairs" only describe the roots. A plural subject needs the plural verb "add up."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Has added up" is singular, but the subject "roots" is plural.
explanation.B: Correct. The plural verb "add up" agrees with the plural subject "roots."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Is adding up" is singular, but the subject "roots" is plural.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Adds up" is singular and would agree with "plant," but the subject is the plural "roots."
